newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ shares end slightly firmer as Telecom gains 7c.
newsitem.headline: NZ shares end slightly firmer as Telecom gains 7c.

text.p: * NZ shares end firmer, Telecom gains on solid volume
* Sky City dips despite 1st half result on expectations
* Good volume in Brierley ahead of half-year result
New Zealand shares ended a touch firmer on Monday, buoyed by seven cent gains in Telecom and in Lion Nathan.
The NZSE-40 Capital Index closed 1.54 points higher at 2,280.87, with Lion Nathan up at $3.63 and Telecom at $6.56.
"Telecom was again the main feature of trade," said Duncan Rutherford at ANZ Securities. "After the recent selling that we've seen, it seems to have found some good buying support."
Telecom has fallen about a dollar since mid-January, predominantly on earnings concerns.

Brokers noted the market leader had struggled up around the $6.60 mark and said there still appeared to be some stock around. There was also a perception now that every time Telecom made a reasonable gain, profit-takers would soon emerge.
Lion's rise was seen purely as a bounce after recent selling pressure, while rural services group Wrightson eased three to $1.04 after recent bidding interest.
The big mover of the day was casino operator Sky City, which plunged 20 cents to $7.00 after reporting an interim profit of $18.2 million.

Brokers said the Sky result was within market expectations but towards the bottom end, and surmised that investors were expecting a full year profit also at the bottom end of forecasts. Sky has forecast a $35.8 million full year result. Brierley Investments, due to report its half year result on Thursday, ended flat at $1.39 on solid turnover worth $6.19 million. Analysts expect the corporate raider to post $100-110 million net profit for the half year, sharply down on last year's $170 million. But they say the company is in good shape, its net tangible asset backing having risen steadily this year to around $1.46 a share. -- Matthew Brockett (64 4) 473-3736
